extracted.intended_audience: artists, art_students, connoisseurs, and readers of art history/biography
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for judging the quality, composition, and execution of Renaissance paintings (exemplified through descriptions of Raffaello's works). Emphasises lifelikeness, composition, draughtsmanship, colour, light, gesture, portraiture, and workshop/design practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity of soul and frank assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: displays the sincerity of soul and frank assurance appropriate to those who live away from the world and despise it, and, in their dealings with mankind, make war on falsehood and speak out the truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures of saints (e.g. S. Jerome) should convey inward devotion and moral character through countenance and posture; the text cites S. Jerome with uplifted head and eyes on the Madonna as exemplifying this sincerity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression suggesting learning and knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: in them seem to be suggested all the learning and knowledge that he showed in his writings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facial expression and bearing ought to communicate intellectual qualities (example: S. Jerome suggested to be learned and knowing by look and pose).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifelike portraiture / verisimilitude
rubrics_metrics.description: which portrait of the Chamberlain is as lifelike as any ever painted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portraits should show convincing likenesses and appear 'as lifelike as any ever painted' (many of Raffaello's portraits—including Popes and courtiers—are singled out as marvellously lifelike).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional tone matching subject
rubrics_metrics.description: glowing with a love in tone with the feeling of the picture, which, both by the lineaments and by the colouring, shows him melting with affection
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colour, line, and gesture must harmonize to express the appropriate emotion (example: S. Francis gazing at the Madonna, where tone and colouring express love and comfort).

rubrics_metrics.name: Beauty and proportion in landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: a landscape, which is singularly beautiful in its absolute perfection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background landscapes should be proportioned and composed to contribute beauty and completeness to the panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychological realism via face and gesture
rubrics_metrics.description: may be perceived in the face of the priest... the shame that he felt... With terror in his eyes, dumbfoundered and beside himself... the gesture of his hands may almost be seen the fear and trembling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paintings should render complex psychological states—shame, terror, bewilderment—through facial expression and hand/ bodily gestures (example: the Mass of Bolsena priest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety and naturalness of figures' movements and gestures
rubrics_metrics.description: many figures, all varied and different, some serving the Mass, others kneeling... making various most beautiful movements and gestures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A composition benefits from a wide range of believable, varied poses and gestures that collectively convey the scene's drama (cited across several fresco scenes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural, womanly grace in figure-turning
rubrics_metrics.description: she... turns in a marvellous manner as she listens to this, with a womanly grace that is very natural and lifelike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subtle turns of the head and body should look spontaneous and graceful rather than artificial; small domestic reactions enhance realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of architectural openings to integrate composition
rubrics_metrics.description: the window-opening he turned to advantage by making a flight of steps, in such a way that all the painting seems to be one whole
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat real architectural elements (windows, steps) as compositional devices to make painted scenes read as cohesive spatial wholes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention and narrative composition
rubrics_metrics.description: in the invention and composition of every kind of painted story, no one has ever been more dexterous, facile, and able than Raffaello.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative scenes should show originality, clear structure, and compositional dexterity—arranging incidents and figures so the story is lucid and engaging (examples: Heliodorus, Attila).

rubrics_metrics.name: Architectural draughtsmanship and judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: he showed such a grasp of architecture, and such judgment in the buildings of the prison
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Buildings and architectural settings should be drawn with correct perspective, proportion, and character, contributing to the scene's believability (example: prison architecture in S. Peter and Herod).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of light, chiaroscuro, and night effects
rubrics_metrics.description: the dazzling splendour of the Angel, which, in the thick darkness of the night, reveals with its light every detail of the prison... the smoke of the torch, the splendour of the Angel, and the thick darkness of the night seem to you to be wholly real and natural
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle multiple light sources, contrasts of light and dark, and atmospheric effects skillfully so illumination reveals form and produces dramatic realism (Mass of Bolsena and S. Peter scenes are given as prime examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rendering of metallic lustre and reflections
rubrics_metrics.description: the blaze of the torch is reflected in all their armour; and all that its glow does not reach is illumined by the light of the moon... their burnished lustre seems more lifelike than if they were real
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paint metal and reflective surfaces with attention to highlights, reflected light, and cast shadows so they appear convincingly metallic and tactile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shadows, projected shadows and vaporous glare
rubrics_metrics.description: shadows playing on the armour, other shadows projected, reflections, and a vaporous glare from the lights, all executed with darkest shade
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use projected shadows, reflected light, and subtle glows to model form and atmosphere; deep darks and subtle tonal transitions increase realism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depiction of belief, guilt, and fervour through pose
rubrics_metrics.description: both men and women... are bewildered by the strangeness... are making various movements... in many, both men and women, there is revealed a belief that they are to blame... the holy Onias... with his eyes and hands raised to Heaven, and praying most fervently
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious and moral responses should be signalled through posture and gesture: raised hands, upturned eyes, kneeling, and group reactions that narrate collective emotional states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective use of portraiture from life
rubrics_metrics.description: he made portraits from nature, also, in some mace-bearers accompanying the Pope, who are marvellously lifelike, as are the horses on which they are riding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When portraying contemporary figures, work from life to capture likeness, costume, and character; realistic portraits can also serve narrative and civic functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressive animal depiction and natural history detail
rubrics_metrics.description: all the animals that Pope Leo possessed, such as the chameleon, the civet-cats, the apes, the parrots, the lions, the elephants, and other beasts even more strange... Giovanni da Udine, his disciple, who has no equal in the painting of animals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animals should be observed and rendered with species-appropriate detail and animation; accurate animal drawing enhances decorative and narrative works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of force and delicacy in colouring
rubrics_metrics.description: painted with such force, and also with a delicacy so pleasing, that I do not think it is possible to do better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colouring should combine vigor (strength of colour, decisive passages) with delicate modulation where required; both qualities together produce superior painting (example: panel for Leonello da Carpi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trompe-l'œil realism of objects and textures
rubrics_metrics.description: musical instruments, which have the appearance of being, not painted, but real and true; and such, also, are some veils that she is wearing, with vestments woven in silk and gold
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict objects—books, instruments, fabrics, metals—with tactile specificity so they read as real items within the picture (examples: S. Cecilia's instruments; Pope's illuminated book; bell of wrought silver).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vitality — the presentation of life
rubrics_metrics.description: other pictures may be said to be pictures, but those of Raffaello life itself, for in his figures the flesh quivers, the very breath may be perceived, the pulse beats, and the true presentment of life is seen in them
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The highest praise is that figures appear alive: subtle modelling, posture, and physiognomy should convey breathing, pulse, and inner life rather than static form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony and unity of colouring
rubrics_metrics.description: the whole being wrought in such a manner that everything reveals spirit, feeling, and thought, and with such a harmony and unity of colouring that nothing better can be conceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colour choices across figures, background, and ornamentation must be unified to produce coherent mood and pictorial harmony (cited for the Papal apartments as a whole).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design transferable across media and to workshop production
rubrics_metrics.description: he drew and coloured with his own hand, of the exact form and size, all the cartoons, which were sent to Flanders to be woven; and the tapestries... were executed so marvellously, that it arouses astonishment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cartoons and designs should be conceived with clarity and scale so they can be successfully translated into other media (tapestry/weaving, engraving) without loss of detail or intention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and veneration of cartoons and drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: this work is in every part so stupendous, that even the cartoons are held in the greatest veneration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality preparatory drawings and cartoons are themselves valuable and should show compositional thought and draughtsmanship worthy of study and preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop organisation and delegation maintaining quality
rubrics_metrics.description: he always kept men who pursued the work from his own designs, while he himself, continually supervising everything, lent to so vast an enterprise the aid of the best efforts of which he was capable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A master should produce designs and supervise execution, employing skilled assistants for ornament, stucco, and execution while ensuring overall artistic unity (examples: Giovanni da Udine, Giulio Romano, others).
